items.title: The Abrahamic covenant is sealed by circumcision

options.text: The covenant between God and Abraham (Genesis 17) promising land and descendants, sealed by circumcision (brit milah) on the eighth day — still observed for Jewish boys today

items.reveal:
Brit milah is performed on the eighth day after birth by a mohel. It marks the Abrahamic covenant (Genesis 17:11-13).

The Mosaic covenant at Sinai (around 1300 BCE in traditional dating) establishes the 613 mitzvot of the Torah law — the framework for Jewish practice.

The Noahide covenant (Genesis 9) applies to all humanity. Rabbinic Judaism distinguishes seven Noahide laws binding on all people from the 613 mitzvot specifically binding on Jews.

Christianity reinterprets these covenants through 'new covenant' theology (Hebrews 8); Judaism rejects supersessionism — the older covenants are not abrogated.
items.why: Covenant is not vague relationship language. In Judaism it is a specific structure with terms, obligations and consequences — and a major point of theological disagreement with Christianity.

items.title: Confucianism is not always classed as a religion

options.text: A monotheistic religion with a creator god

An ethical and philosophical tradition centred on social relationships and self-cultivation — often called a religion in Western frameworks but treated as philosophy and ethics in Chinese tradition; rituals (li) and the cultivation of virtues (ren, yi, zhi, xin) are central

items.reveal:
Confucius (Kongzi, 551-479 BCE) taught a system of social ethics based on five key relationships: ruler-subject, parent-child, husband-wife, elder-younger sibling, friend-friend. Filial piety (xiao) anchors the family; ren (humaneness) and li (ritual propriety) anchor the broader ethical life.

The Analects (Lunyu) is the foundational text, compiled by disciples. Mencius (4th century BCE) and Xunzi (3rd century BCE) developed the tradition. Neo-Confucianism (Zhu Xi, 12th century) systematised it for later imperial China.

Whether Confucianism is a religion depends on the definition of religion — it includes ritual, sage veneration and cosmological elements but no creator god or afterlife doctrine.
items.why: Western categories ('religion', 'philosophy', 'ethics') don't always fit non-Western traditions. Confucianism's case shows how the very question of what counts as religion is partly a cultural artefact — and changes the answer.

items.title: British religious affiliation has dropped sharply since the 1960s
items.claim: What does the 2021 UK Census show about religion?

options.text: For the first time, less than half of England and Wales (46.2%) identified as Christian; 37.2% had no religion; Islam grew to 6.5%; Hindu, Sikh, Jewish, Buddhist and Other religions made up the remainder
All religions are at the same percentage

items.reveal:
The 2001 Census recorded 72% Christian; 2011 recorded 59%; 2021 recorded 46% in England and Wales. The 'no religion' category rose from 15% (2001) to 25% (2011) to 37% (2021). Scotland (2022 census) showed similar trends; Northern Ireland remains more religious.

Muslim population: 3% (2001), 5% (2011), 6.5% (2021).

Secularisation theory (Bryan Wilson, Peter Berger) predicted declining religious influence with modernity. The reality has been more complex — declining institutional affiliation alongside persistent or growing 'spiritual but not religious' identification and increasing pluralism.
items.why: British religion is restructured, not just declining. The Census numbers show a more religiously plural country where institutional Christianity has lost its majority position — major implications for education, ethics and public life.
